title: Service-claim policy compiler, KMS zone attestor, and audit-seal
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context and motivation: Customers requested safer migration from legacy service-role YAMLs to RBAC v2 while ensuring KMS usage remains constrained to validated zones and audit logs carry an immutable proof header. This PR implements a service-claim policy compiler (to generate least-privilege RBAC v2 roles from existing service claim manifests), a KMS zone attestor middleware that verifies incoming requests contain a short-lived zone attestation token, and an audit-seal generator that appends an HMAC-style seal to audit events derived from a transient CMK-wrapped nonce. Goals: 1) Make RBAC policy migration automated and auditable; 2) Ensure KMS operations are bound to declared zone attestations at the per-request level; 3) Provide an immutable, small footprint audit seal for downstream retention and tamper-evidence.

What changed (high level): Compiles service claim declarations into RBAC v2 RoleBindings + conditions; adds a new middleware path in the API gateway (authn/authz) for KMS zone attestation verification; introduces an audit-seal step in the audit pipeline that signs event envelopes using a short-lived nonce created by the customer CMK via the KMS proxy; includes end-to-end integration tests and a lightweight policy-lint tool to validate generated roles.

Single-line summary of commits: feat(compiler): add claim->rbacv2 compiler; feat(kms): implement zone attestation verifier; feat(audit): add sealed-audit-enveloper; test: integration tests for compiler+attestor+seal; docs: usage guide and migration notes; ci: add e2e job for sealed-audit.

Changed areas / files (high level): src/policy/compiler/* (compiler core, heuristics, test cases); api/gateway/middleware/kmz_attestor.go (attestor implementation + caching layer); audit/enveloper/seal.go (seal generator + verification helpers); tools/policy-lint/ (CLI to lint generated roles); docs/security/claim-migration.md (migration guide); tests/integration/claim_kms_seal_test.go (end-to-end scenarios); chart/templates/gateway-config.yaml (feature flag and config knobs).

Implementation notes and tradeoffs: The compiler uses a conservative heuristic to prefer deny-by-default and only emits allow conditions directly referenced by service claims. We intentionally avoid full semantic inference (too risky) and instead emit an annotated policy with a migration-warning section. The KMS zone attestor expects an attestation token signed by our attestation service; to keep latency low we cache attestation validation results for 30s and fall back to realtime verification on cache-miss. The audit-seal uses CMK-derived nonces (GenerateDataKey-like flow) to avoid exposing raw CMKs; the seal size is intentionally small (96 bytes) to keep event storage costs reasonable while preserving tamper-evidence when combined with the existing audit chain hash.

Security review summary: Diego performed threat modeling focusing on token replay, operator escalation, and KMS misuse. Mitigations include short TTLs for attestation tokens, nonce single-use checks at the audit ingress, and RBAC compiler warnings to disallow generating cluster-admin level bindings. Sophie validated policy generation against our test corpus of 300 internal services; none required manual widening of permissions beyond the compiler suggestions.

Testing and CI: Added unit tests for the compiler heuristics, property-based tests for attestation token parsing, and an integration job that provisions a test KMS key and runs a full request path (authn -> attestor -> kms proxy -> audit seal). CI summary: initial run had a flaky attestor cache race on linux-arm which was fixed in the second commit; final CI status green (all checks passed).

Migration and rollout plan: Feature gated behind security.feature.claim_policy_compiler. Rollout phases: canary (5% of requests) with compiler disabled (only emits dry-run diagnostics), opt-in for policy application via admin API, then automatic application for services that pass linting for two consecutive runs. KMS attestor gate defaults to off; enable only after attestation-key rollout and customer opt-in. Audit-seal enabled by default for new accounts, opt-in for existing accounts with retention considerations.

Review conversation (high level; truncated): "Diego: please confirm replay protection for attestation tokens; add tests." "Author (Maya): added nonce single-use check and e2e test." "Jasper: policy-lint CLI looks good — one nit on output formatting." "Sophie: approved after test refresh and docs updates." No outstanding changes requested at merge time.

Release notes: "Add service-claim to RBAC v2 policy compiler; optional KMS zone attestation middleware; audit-seal for tamper-evidence. See docs/security/claim-migration.md for migration steps and rollout options."

Operational impact: Adds a small in-memory cache in the gateway (default 30s) and an additional KMS GenerateDataKey call when seals are emitted (batched for high-throughput paths). Estimated cost impact: +0.6% per 1M requests when audit-seal enabled (based on KMS pricing model). Performance: median p95 increase for auth path ~8ms on canary; mitigations documented in the rollout guide.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI. Follow-ups: SEC-820 add attestation key rotation tooling; ENG-4898 make cache configurable per-tenant; DOC-901 expand migration examples for legacy YAMLs.
